title: async and await
summary: Write promise-based code that reads top to bottom using async functions, await and try...catch.

quiz.q: What does an async function always return?
quiz.explain: Even if you `return 5`, the caller receives a promise that fulfills with 5. That is why callers use `await` or `.then`.

quiz.q: Click the line that must change so that both `await` lines work.
quiz.explain: `await` can only be used inside an `async` function. The first line should read `async function getTotal(...)`.

quiz.q: What does this program print? Write the two words separated by a space.
quiz.explain: `await` pauses `run` and lets the rest of the program continue, so `after` prints before `end`.

quiz.q: Complete the code so a rejected promise does not crash the function.
quiz.explain: A rejected promise that you `await` throws an error at that line, so ordinary `try...catch` handles it.

quiz.q: You need two independent results and want them as fast as possible. Which is best?
options: await one, then await the other
quiz.explain: `Promise.all` starts both at once and waits for both. Two awaits in a row make the second wait for the first for no reason.

exercise.task:
In `asyncawait.js`, write three `async` functions. Each receives functions that return promises (called loaders):

- `addAsync(loadA, loadB)` awaits both loaders and returns the sum of their results.
- `safeLoad(load, fallback)` awaits `load()`. If it rejects, return `fallback` instead (use `try...catch`).
- `loadAll(loaders)` takes an array of loaders, runs them all at the same time with `Promise.all`, and returns the array of results.
hints: Write `async function name(...) { ... }` and put `await` in front of every loader call.
For `safeLoad`, wrap the `await` in `try { ... } catch (error) { ... }`. For `loadAll`, map the loaders to promises: `loaders.map((load) => load())`.
